Nine comments

This is the first tune on Lunasa’s second album. Lovely flowing rhthm. It reminds me a bit of “George White’s Favourite”.

↳ Posted by Ah, Surely! on July 8th, 2001.

Composer

Since the ABC Input routine cuts of any additional abc tags such as composer, transcriber, etc. here is the composer of this lovely tune. It’s Lunasa’s guitar player Donogh Hennessy.

↳ Posted by Ah, Surely! on July 11th, 2001.

Comments

That’s the idea: to add information like composer, transcriber, etc. here in the comments. That’s kind of why you have the option to add comments in the first place. There is also a link under “Details” to add alternate titles.

I don’t want to get technical, but basically because of the way The Session database works, the ABC notation must remain quite straightforward - the basic headers, followed by the body of the tune. I decided not to include a header for composer as most tunes are traditional.

Personally, I think it’s also a lot nicer to read information about composers, transcribers, etc. in full sentences rather than ABC headers.

↳ Posted by Jeremy on July 11th, 2001.

Re: Goodbye Miss Goodavich

According to a Lúnasa source, this song was written by Donogh Hennessy for a woman he met in Australia: Lara Goodridge, an Australian fiddler and singer. You can find her discography here:
https://www.discogs.com/artist/353779-Lara-Goodridge
and information on some of her bands (Fourplay: https://www.fourplay.com.au), Baby et Lulu (https://www.babyetlulu.com.au)

↳ Posted by BansheeWailsOverTheMangoPit on March 13th, 2021.

Re: Goodbye Miss Goodavich

Somebody at my local session yesterday told me with great authority that this tune was written by Michael McGoldrick and Miss Goodavitch was his former landlady in Manchester. ‘Fake news’ of course, and I corrected him. But I wonder where some of these myths come from.

One of my favorite examples of tune misappropriation is the story that Willie Coleman did not actually write Willie Coleman’s jig (Martin Wynne did).

Anyhow we need to make sure that Donagh Hennessy retains the credit for his own tunes in the face of the tide of McGoldrickitis

↳ Posted by Edgar Bolton on June 5th, 2025.
